top_stories.title: Fed Poised for First Rate Hike Since 2023
points: Fed widely expected to raise rates 25 basis points (0.25%) today to 3.75%-4.00%, marking first hike since mid-2023.
CME FedWatch tool showed 92-93% probability of a hike priced in ahead of the 2 p.m. ET decision.
Decision comes despite President Trump's public pressure for rate cuts, raising Fed independence concerns.
New Fed Chair Kevin Warsh opposes forward guidance (signaling future rate direction), so FOMC statement will focus only on today's move, followed by a 2:30 p.m. press conference.

Strong jobs data and inflation stuck above the 2% target provide the economic rationale, though critics warn of stagflation risk (slow growth plus high inflation) since the hike doesn't address root causes like oil prices and geopolitical shocks.
10-year Treasury yield has climbed to its highest level since 2007 on hike expectations, with some forecasts seeing yields reach 4.5%.

Historically, S&P 500 has averaged negative returns in the four months after a Fed hike before turning positive; 12-month average return post-hike is 6.7% (median 10.7%) across six tightening cycles since 1994, suggesting the hike alone is unlikely to derail the bull market.

Stock futures/markets have been choppy into the decision: S&P 500, Dow, and Nasdaq each fell 0.5-0.8% in the run-up, while futures rose after two prior down days; Bank of America separately warns stocks look 'overdue' for a pullback.
Sector impact expected to diverge: bank stocks seen benefiting from wider lending margins, while tech and growth stocks face pressure from higher discount rates on future cash flows.

unique_angles.point: Weekly jobless claims (Thursday) and core inflation data (Friday, any reading above 0.3% monthly) flagged as the key catalysts that could still tip the Fed's hand.
Some FOMC governors reportedly remain unconvinced, leaving a small chance of a last-minute vote change despite the outcome appearing largely predetermined.
Analysts stress that what happens after the Fed's decision matters more for long-term market direction than the announcement itself.

top_stories.title: Iran Conflict and Related Military Costs Mount
points: Congressional Budget Office estimates the Iran war has cost U.S. taxpayers $38 billion, with U.S. missile interceptor supplies now depleted from defending against Iranian attacks.
Trump administration's naval blockade of Iran is costing the Pentagon roughly $32.5 million per day, straining U.S. military capacity globally.
Separate estimate puts total Iran conflict costs at $246 million per day over its first five months.
U.S. is finalizing a $2.8 billion bomb sale to Israel, described as the largest weapons sale in years.

unique_angles.point: Saudi Arabia is ramping up crude spot sales from ports outside the Strait of Hormuz after an East-West pipeline shutdown, adapting its export strategy to the tensions.
Bank of Japan is separately expected to hike rates to a 30-year high, adding another global monetary policy data point this week.

top_stories.title: Crypto Regulation Setback: Clarity Act Stalls
points: The Clarity Act, a bill meant to establish clear cryptocurrency regulatory rules, failed to advance in the Senate, leaving the industry's legal framework unresolved.
Bitcoin fell roughly 1.3% to about $75,915 on the news, dragging down crypto-linked stocks.
Concerns over President Trump's personal crypto investments were cited as a factor in the bill's collapse.

unique_angles.point: Two Robinhood engineers were separately charged with insider trading on crypto-linked perpetual futures (derivative contracts with no expiry date that track an underlying asset's price), adding to industry legal troubles.

top_stories.title: AI Industry Investment and Safety Debate Continues
points: OpenAI is reportedly seeking new funding at a $1.2 trillion valuation, which could let it delay an IPO and fund further acquisitions.

Meta's Mark Zuckerberg and Nvidia's Jensen Huang pushed back on claims of an AI slowdown, defending continued heavy investment in AI infrastructure, while Zuckerberg also called for AI labs to use independent safety evaluators.

OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google DeepMind have reportedly been coordinating for weeks on AI safety measures, prompting FTC Chair Andrew Ferguson to warn he'd be 'deeply suspicious' of companies seeking antitrust exemptions (legal permission to cooperate despite normal competition rules) under the guise of safety.
Senior U.S. officials met with Anthropic to discuss AI risks, signaling rising government attention to the sector.

unique_angles.point: Critics question the safety-coordination truce as possible competitive collusion disguised as a safety initiative, amid employee whistleblower warnings.
The AI boom is creating unexpected billionaires in unglamorous manufacturing niches like drawer slides and micro drill bits, showing the boom's reach beyond chipmakers.

items.title: Semiconductor Supply Chain Diversification
points: SK Hynix is reportedly in talks with Intel to manufacture memory chips (DRAM, a common type of computer memory) in U.S. facilities, which would be the first domestic production partnership between the two companies.

items.title: Other Market and Infrastructure Notes
points: AWS still hasn't restored service to its Bahrain and UAE data centers following an earlier outage.
Enbridge reopened its Line 5 pipeline and launched an 'open season' (a bidding process for shipping capacity) for a proposed Texas pipeline expansion.
Russia and Ukraine continue targeting each other's oil infrastructure despite Trump's claims otherwise, keeping energy prices elevated and adding inflationary pressure.

items.title: Oil Supply and Treasury Policy Pressures
points: Oil prices held above $106/barrel as Houthi strikes and Saudi pipeline outages threatened disruption of up to 4% of global supply.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent faced congressional pressure over a failed $6 billion bond buyback program and the administration's unexplained plan to fund a proposed $5,000 taxpayer dividend without new congressional spending.

items.title: Trump Administration's Corporate Investment Deals Underperform
points: Of 17 public companies that struck investment deals involving the Trump administration, 14 are now trading below their initial announcement-day prices.
Typical pattern: a stock 'sugar high' bump on announcement day followed by high volatility and rapid loss of those gains.
Only 6 of 17 companies show positive returns versus prices from 10 trading days before the announcement, meaning most investors who anticipated the deals would still be underwater.
Policy analyst Tad DeHaven notes long-term returns depend on business fundamentals, not government backing.

items.title: Musk Floats Possible Tesla-SpaceX Merger
points: At the All-In Summit, Elon Musk hinted at a possible merger between Tesla and SpaceX, citing extensive collaboration across personnel, technology, and products.
The companies are already intertwined: Tesla holds equity in SpaceX, SpaceX buys Tesla batteries and Cybertrucks, and Tesla embeds SpaceX's Grok AI in vehicles.
A merger would eliminate the option to invest in the two companies separately, forcing investors to buy the combined entity or exit.

items.title: EU Offers Canada Associate Membership
points: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen invited Canada to become the EU's first associate member, as part of a push to expand partnerships beyond traditional structures.

Canadian PM Mark Carney has repeatedly said the 'rules-based international order' is dead and is urging middle powers (smaller countries with outsized influence) to coordinate as a counterweight to major powers.

items.title: US Diesel Prices Hit Record High
points: Drone strikes on Russian refineries and shipping disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz (a waterway carrying about 20% of global oil) pushed U.S. diesel above $6 per gallon for the first time ever last week.
U.S. diesel stockpiles are projected to fall this month to their lowest level in 20 years, threatening heating oil costs this fall.
The price surge is hitting farmers in Iowa and Kansas during harvest season and other Trump 2024 voters, creating political risk ahead of midterm elections.

items.title: Other Financial Planning Notes
points: About a quarter of Americans claim Social Security at age 62, significantly reducing their lifetime benefits.
An analysis of 31 college majors shows vastly different job growth prospects through 2034.

issues.subject: Morning Brief: Get ready for a Fed hike — and market turbulence

headlines: Federal Reserve poised to raise interest rates for first time since 2023 as inflation concerns resurface; CME futures show 92% probability of hike at 2 p.m. ET decision.
U.S. 10-year Treasury yield hits highest level since 2007, spooking investors as bond market signals economic stress.
Major AI companies OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google DeepMind agree to collaborate on safety measures amid escalating public concerns about AI risks.
Trump administration's investment portfolio underperforming: 14 of 17 public companies that struck deals now trading below initial announcement prices.
Elon Musk hints at possible merger of Tesla and SpaceX, citing extensive collaboration across personnel, technology, and products between companies.

sections.title: 1. Federal Reserve Rate Hike Decision Looms
points: CME futures market pricing in 92% probability of rate increase, marking first hike since 2023 after Iran-related geopolitical disruptions stalled inflation progress.
Decision arrives at 2 p.m. ET with dot plot (forward guidance projections from Federal Reserve officials), followed by Chair Kevin Warsh's press conference at 2:30 p.m.
Some FOMC governors reportedly remain unconvinced, creating possibility for last-minute vote changes before the meeting, though outcome appears largely predetermined.
Rising Treasury yields already spooking equity investors; S&P 500 fell 0.5%, Dow 0.6%, and Nasdaq 0.8% in lead-up to announcement.

sections.title: 2. AI Industry Coordination on Safety Raises Competitive Concerns
points: OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google DeepMind have been working together for several weeks on AI safety measures, following high-profile warnings from Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and endorsement from OpenAI's Sam Altman.

FTC Chair Andrew Ferguson warned Tuesday he would be 'deeply suspicious' of AI companies seeking antitrust exemptions (legal permission to work together despite usual competition rules) to coordinate on safety.
Public concern over AI's economic and security threats has reached inflection point, with employee whistleblowers and industry leaders calling for collective development slowdown.
Critics question motives behind industry truce, viewing coordination as potential competitive collusion disguised as safety initiative.

sections.title: 3. Trump Administration Investment Portfolio Severely Underperforming
points: Analysis shows 14 of 17 public companies accepting government involvement ended the week with stock prices lower than the day after deal announcements were made.

Most companies experienced classic pattern: significant stock bump on announcement day, high volatility afterward, then rapid loss of gains, suggesting short-term 'sugar high' rather than fundamental improvement.

Only 6 of 17 companies show positive returns when compared to prices 10 trading days before formal announcement, indicating majority of investors would be underwater even if they anticipated the deal.
Policy analyst Tad DeHaven notes long-term returns depend on fundamentals rather than government support, contradicting narrative that federal backing guarantees stock success.

sections.title: 4. Musk Discusses Potential Tesla-SpaceX Merger
points: At All-In Summit, Musk suggested merging his major enterprises, stating: 'With all this collaboration, on so many levels, who can imagine what action one might take when there's so much close collaboration.'
Companies already deeply intertwined: Tesla holds equity stake in SpaceX, SpaceX purchases Tesla batteries and Cybertrucks, and Tesla embeds SpaceX's Grok AI technology into vehicles.
Earlier reports indicated Musk discussed merger possibility before SpaceX's June IPO; topic resurfaced during Q2 earnings call but Musk stopped short of confirmation.

Merger would eliminate separate investment option in Musk empire, forcing retail investors to buy combined entity or exit entirely, potentially justifying deal through new synergies and growth prospects.
